- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for early horizon (1–7 days) and 20–50% for longer horizon (8–30 days).  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates prices; increase forecast by 10–30% for early horizon, and 20–40% for longer horizon.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 2.12→2.03), producing exaggerated downward forecasts in next 3–7 days; cap forecast decline at 10–20% below peak.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days are above 2.00, forecast tends to overshoot downward; adjust by adding 0.10–0.30 to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.05–0.15 to forecast for days 15–30.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.50, -0.33), model underestimates true drop; apply 10–20% upward adjustment to forecast for 1–5 days after negative sentiment.
